name: Bench Harbor

# Runs the fa coding agent against the Terminal-Bench dataset family on
# the Harbor framework: 2.0 / 2.1 / 3.0 / 4.0 from ONE dispatch surface
# (issue #1124; the 4.0 path is issue #147). The `dataset` input takes a
# family label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or a full Harbor dataset id — resolved
# and validated by bench/harbor_fa/families.py (unknown or version-less
# specs fail fast; never a silent fallback). The default dispatch is the
# 2.1 family (issue #1316: the bench migrates to Terminal-Bench 2.x /
# Harbor — supersedes #1124 AC4's 4.0 default; 4.0/3.0/2.0 stay one input
# away). CPU shards run the default Harbor `docker` sandbox on
# ubuntu-latest (GH runners ship docker — no Modal/cloud dependency for
# the default dispatch, #1316); GPU tasks always route to a modal shard
# and cpu-runner/cpu-env keep the self-hosted + modal dispatch reachable.
# Results upload
# to Harbor Hub — the current leaderboard source (tbench.ai; 4.0 is the
# leaderboard dataset). The legacy terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 path lives
# in bench.yml.
#
# Same bundle/env contract as the legacy bench: `dart build cli` Linux
# bundle + an env-provider-preconfig, secrets env-only and never echoed
# (keys pass base64-encoded into the task container; CI masks both raw
# and base64 forms).
#
# gh-1503: the provider is no longer a z.ai hardcode — the dispatch
# picks zai glm-5.3-flash (default, byte-identical to the pre-gh-1503
# wiring), kimi-for-coding k3-256k (FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY), or `custom`
# (provider-config JSON validated in the resolve step; key only from
# FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY). The setup job's resolve step is a byte-consistent
# copy of bench.yml's gh-1471 step — keep both in sync (cross-reference
# comment in both files). With the z.ai budget at zero, the kimi path is
# what keeps this workflow dispatchable.
#
# Smoke first: dispatch with tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1 (smoke task
# per family in docs/bench.md). Full (tasks-less) runs of the
# intermediate families (2.0/2.1/3.0) additionally require
# confirm-full-run: true — a full family sweep is hours of GPU + LLM
# spend. Full 4.0 dispatches keep their historical no-confirmation
# behaviour (issue #1124 AC4).
#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY       — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
#   FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY      — kimi coding key for k3-256k (shared with bench.yml;
#                            never the review factory's KIMI_REVIEW_KEY)
#   FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY    — key for provider=custom, injected as FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
#   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET  — Modal token for the GPU shard (verified live)
#   HARBOR_API_KEY         — Harbor Hub upload key; upload step skips (with a
#                            warning) when absent, run artifacts keep results.

run-name: fa bench-harbor · ${{ inputs.provider }} · ${{ inputs.tasks }}

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset (empty = full dataset; use the family smoke task first — docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1503, same contract as bench.yml gh-1471: default = pre-gh-1503 behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret; custom needs FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY + provider-config)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
          - 'custom'
      provider-config:
        description: 'gh-1503 (bench.yml gh-1471 D1/AC 2a): ONLY when provider=custom — the provider config JSON {"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}. The API key NEVER rides this input (run metadata is visible) — it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Terminal-Bench family: label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or full Harbor id (see bench/harbor_fa/families.py); default 2.1 (issue #1316)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest'
      confirm-full-run:
        description: 'Required true for full (tasks-less) runs of 2.0/2.1/3.0 — smoke first (docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false

def _resolve_run_block() -> str:
    """Extracts the `run: |` block of the provider resolve step.

    Same text-slicing contract as bench/terminal_bench/test_bench_workflow.py
    (_resolve_run_block): the block is identified by its body (the
    provider_config printf), so unrelated `run:` blocks never match. The
    block is env-driven (inputs/secrets arrive via the step env), so no
    GitHub expression may appear inside.
    """
    lines = _HARBOR_YML.read_text().splitlines()
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if line.strip() != "run: |":
            continue
        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
        body = []
        for candidate in lines[i + 1 :]:
            if candidate.strip() and (len(candidate) - len(candidate.lstrip())) <= indent:
                break
            body.append(candidate)
        while body and not body[-1].strip():
            body.pop()
        block = "\n".join(body)
        if "provider_config=$(printf" in block:
            break
    else:
        raise AssertionError("provider resolve step's run: | block not found in bench-harbor.yml")
    leftover = re.findall(r"\$\{\{[^}]*\}\}", block)
    assert not leftover, f"unmapped GitHub expression(s) in resolve block: {leftover}"
    return block

              # shard-hours failing loud inside every trial.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — the raw input is not echoed (it could carry key material)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `apiKeyEnvVar` is injected by this step (fixed
              # FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM), never accepted from the input — a
              # user-supplied value would be silently overridden (checked
              # before the key-like scan below, which would otherwise
              # flag the field first with a less precise message).
              if printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'has("apiKeyEnvVar")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not declare apiKeyEnvVar — the resolve step injects it as the fixed FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM; the key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Key-like fields hard-fail: a pasted key in a dispatch
              # input would leak through run metadata. Whole-word match
              # on the key's split words (camelCase/snake_case divided) —
              # so the legitimate `maxTokens` capability key passes while
              # `token`/`accessToken`/`api_key` are caught. The scan
              # descends into nested objects: a key field name pasted
              # inside a header map rides through a top-level-only scan
              # exactly like a top-level one.
              leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                def words: gsub("(?<l>[a-z0-9])(?<u>[A-Z])"; "\(.l)_\(.u)")
                  | gsub("[ _-]+"; " ") | ascii_downcase | split(" ");
                [.. | objects | keys[]
                  | select(. | words
                      | map(test("^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$"))
                      | any)]
                  | unique | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$leaked" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not carry key material — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata; offending field(s): $leaked. The key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Closed key whitelist, mirroring the Dart _parseConfig
              # consumer (baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar, contextWindow,
              # maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel): an unknown or typo'd
              # key would otherwise fail loud at every trial's container
              # boot after shards start. `type` is allowed here (it rides
              # the FA_PROVIDER_TYPE output) but stripped from the
              # emitted config below.
              unsupported=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                [. | keys[]
                  | select(. as $k
                      | ["baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens","input","thinkingLevel","type"]
                      | index($k) | not)]
                  | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$unsupported" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config has unsupported key(s): $unsupported — supported keys: baseUrl, model, contextWindow, maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel (type selects FA_PROVIDER_TYPE and is not echoed into FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `type` feeds the container's catalog lookup via
              # FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: when declared it must be a non-empty
              # string (jq's `//` treats "" as present, so an explicit
              # check is required); undeclared/null defaults to the
              # openai-compatible catalog entry.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'if has("type") and .type != null then (.type | type == "string" and test("\\S")) else true end' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config \"type\" must be a non-empty string naming a catalog provider (e.g. \"openai\") when declared"; exit 1
              fi
              # The capability pair mirrors _parseCapabilityInt: JSON
              # integers at or above the Dart resolver floors
              # (minOverrideContextWindow 16384 / minOverrideMaxTokens
              # 1024 — the same boundaries as the yaml overrides layer);
              # blank string / null are ABSENT, like every other optional
              # input; anything else throws at container boot today.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '
                def capok(min): . as $v
                  | $v == null or (($v | type) == "string" and ($v | test("^\\s*$")))
                  or (($v | type) == "number" and ($v | floor) == $v and $v >= min);
                (.contextWindow | capok(16384)) and (.maxTokens | capok(1024))
              ' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config contextWindow/maxTokens must be integers at or above the Dart resolver floors (contextWindow >= 16384, maxTokens >= 1024) — a below-floor or non-integer declaration would fail loud at every trial's container boot"; exit 1
              fi
              # `input` mirrors _parseInputList: a non-empty list whose
              # entries are exactly "text"/"image".
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'if has("input") then (.input | type == "array" and length > 0 and all(.[]; . == "text" or . == "image")) else true end' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config \"input\" must be a non-empty list of \"text\"/\"image\" entries (the Dart preconfig's contract)"; exit 1
              fi
              # `thinkingLevel` mirrors _parseThinkingLevel: a blank
              # string is absent; otherwise one of the
              # configThinkingLevels ladder (xhigh/max fold to high
              # Dart-side).
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'if has("thinkingLevel") then (.thinkingLevel | if type == "string" then (test("^\\s*$") or (. as $l | ["minimal","low","medium","high","xhigh","max"] | index($l) != null)) else false end) else true end' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config \"thinkingLevel\" must be one of minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max (the Dart preconfig's ladder)"; exit 1
              fi
              # Required: a non-empty https:// baseUrl and a model — the
              # plain-http ban keeps the bench key off a cleartext wire.
              for field in baseUrl model; do
                if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e --arg f "$field" '.[$f] | type == "string" and length > 0' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                  echo "::error::provider-config is missing a non-empty \"$field\" — required: baseUrl, model"; exit 1
                fi
              done
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '.baseUrl | startswith("https://")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config baseUrl must start with https:// (a plaintext endpoint would expose the bench key) — got: $(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.baseUrl')"; exit 1
              fi
              # Passthrough: every declared field rides the config
              # verbatim EXCEPT "type" — it already rides the dedicated
              # FA_PROVIDER_TYPE output/env, and the Dart preconfig's
              # FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG whitelist has no "type" key (it would
              # throw at every trial's container boot). Blank/null
              # capability fields are dropped (Dart-side they are
              # ABSENT, like every other optional input — the emitted
              # config declares only what is effective). Plus the fixed
              # key-env injection; `type` defaults to the
              # openai-compatible catalog entry.
              provider_type=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.type // "openai"')
              model=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.model')
              provider_config=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -c --arg k "$key_env" '
                del(.type)
                | del(.contextWindow | select(. == null or ((. | type) == "string" and (. | test("^\\s*$")))))
                | del(.maxTokens | select(. == null or ((. | type) == "string" and (. | test("^\\s*$")))))
                | . + {apiKeyEnvVar: $k}')
              run_label="custom ($model)"
              ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::unknown provider '$PROVIDER' — expected 'zai-glm-5.3-flash', 'kimi-for-coding' or 'custom'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ -z "$secret_value" ]; then
            echo "::error::provider $PROVIDER selected but secret $secret_name is not set"; exit 1
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded;
          # GitHub auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$secret_value" | base64 -w0)"
          {
            echo "provider_type=$provider_type"
            echo "provider_config=$provider_config"
            echo "provider_key_env=$key_env"
            echo "bench_model=$model"
            echo "run_label=$run_label"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # stable satisfies the repo SDK constraint (>=3.12.0 <4.0.0).
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - run: dart pub get

      # Resolve the dispatch input (family label, bare version, or full
      # Harbor id) to the canonical dataset id; unknown or version-less
      # specs fail fast here, before any download.
      - name: Resolve Terminal-Bench family
        id: family
        env:
          DATASET: ${{ inputs.dataset }}
        run: python bench/harbor_fa/families.py resolve "$DATASET"

      # Cost guard (issue #1124 E3): full runs of the intermediate
      # families are hours of GPU + LLM spend — require explicit
      # confirmation. Smoke runs (non-empty tasks) and 4.0 (the
      # historical default, AC4) are unaffected.
      - name: Confirm full intermediate-family run
        if: steps.family.outputs.family != '4.0' && inputs.confirm-full-run != true
        env:
          TASKS: ${{ inputs.tasks }}
          ATTEMPTS: ${{ inputs.attempts }}
        run: |
          # split_tasks.py strips each comma-glob before use, so " ", ",",
          # " , " all normalize to zero globs = a FULL dataset run. Judge
          # emptiness on that same normalization, not the raw input.
          if [ -z "$(printf %s "$TASKS" | tr -d '[:space:],')" ]; then
            echo "::error::Full run of Terminal-Bench ${{ steps.family.outputs.family }} (${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}, ~${{ steps.family.outputs.tasks }} tasks x $ATTEMPTS attempts) requires confirm-full-run: true. Smoke first: tasks=${{ steps.family.outputs.smoke }}, attempts=1 (docs/bench.md)."
            exit 1
          fi

      # Same bundle as bench/terminal_bench/run.sh: tar the bundle/ dir so
      # the adapter extracts bin/fah at the top level of /opt/fa.
      - name: Build fa CLI bundle (Linux)
        run: |
          bundle_dir="$(mktemp -d)/fa-bundle"
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output="$bundle_dir"
          tar -czf fa-bundle.tar.gz -C "$bundle_dir/bundle" .

      - name: Upload fa bundle
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-bundle
          path: fa-bundle.tar.gz

      # terminal-bench-era note: harbor is fine on 3.13; typer-based CLIs
      # break on 3.14.
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # Pinned: the adapter targets the 0.23.0 BaseInstalledAgent contract.
      - run: pip install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0'

      # Same gate as bench.yml: stdlib-only bench script tests. Two
      # discovery roots: bench/terminal_bench (legacy scripts + the
      # harbor parity suite from #1122 — terminal-bench is installed
      # just for the legacy-adapter import surface) and bench/harbor_fa
      # (the #1124 family/summary suites + the #1123 token/cost summary
      # tests). Discovering bench/ itself would need __init__.py
      # plumbing the bench dirs don't have.
      - name: Unit-test bench scripts
        run: |
          pip install 'terminal-bench==0.2.18'
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v

      # Download the dataset once for classification; harbor re-fetches
      # into its own cache during the run. DATASET is the canonical id
      # resolved by the family step (the raw input may be a bare label).
      - name: Shard dataset into CPU / GPU shards
        id: shards
        env:
          DATASET: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
          TASKS: ${{ inputs.tasks }}
          SHARDS: ${{ inputs.shards }}
          CPU_ENV: ${{ inputs.cpu-env }}
        run: |
          harbor datasets download "$DATASET" --output-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/ds" --overwrite
          # Dataset name at version: dir name is the dataset slug.
          ds_dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/ds/$(basename "${DATASET%%@*}")"
          [ -d "$ds_dir" ] || ds_dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/ds"
          # split_tasks.py writes the matrix/counts into GITHUB_OUTPUT itself.
          # harbor -i matches qualified ids (<org>/<name>): prefix with the
          # org part of the dataset spec.
          python bench/harbor_fa/split_tasks.py "$ds_dir" \
            --filter "$TASKS" --shards "$SHARDS" --cpu-env "$CPU_ENV" \
            --task-prefix "${DATASET%%/*}/"

  bench:
    name: fa on tbench ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}, shard ${{ matrix.i }} (${{ matrix.env }}, ${{ needs.setup.outputs.run_label }})
    needs: setup
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.cpu-runner }}
    # ~4 tasks/shard x --n-attempts x task runtime (tbench agent caps
    # reach 8h but typical runs are far shorter) with headroom; the
    # self-hosted runner has no 6h hosted-runner cap to trip over.
    timeout-minutes: 355
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      max-parallel: 5
      matrix: ${{ fromJSON(needs.setup.outputs.matrix) }}
    env:
      FAMILY: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}
      DATASET: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.dataset }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Download fa bundle
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-bundle

      # The optional self-hosted runner is a macOS box: setup-python cannot
      # write the hosted tool cache there (mkdir /Users/runner denied) and the
      # runner's own python3 is 3.14 — typer-based CLIs (harbor) break on 3.14.
      # The uv-managed CPython 3.13 user-space install below works on BOTH
      # runner kinds (the ubuntu-latest default included); uv is also the
      # canonical harbor install per the 4.0 docs.
      - name: Install harbor (uv-managed python 3.13)
        run: |
          export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
          command -v uv >/dev/null || curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
          export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
          uv venv --python 3.13 .bench-venv
          uv pip install --python .bench-venv/bin/python 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0'
          .bench-venv/bin/python -c 'import sys; print("venv python:", sys.version.split()[0])'

      - name: Run harbor (fa agent, ${{ matrix.env }} env)
        env:
          FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-bundle.tar.gz
          PYTHONPATH: ${{ github.workspace }}/bench/harbor_fa
          # gh-1503: the provider triple is resolved once in the setup
          # job (preflighted secret + hard fail on an unmapped choice) —
          # the shard only consumes it. All three bench keys are mapped
          # here (custom's AC 2a: key only from FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY); the
          # run block picks the resolved one by name, fa_agent.py ships
          # exactly that key into the container.
          FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.provider_type }}
          FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.provider_config }}
          FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.provider_key_env }}
          FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
          MODAL_TOKEN_ID: ${{ secrets.MODAL_TOKEN_ID }}
          MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET: ${{ secrets.MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET }}
          HARBOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.HARBOR_API_KEY }}
          MODEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.bench_model }}
          ATTEMPTS: ${{ inputs.attempts }}
          NCONC: ${{ inputs.n-concurrent }}
          ENV_TYPE: ${{ matrix.env }}
          # No step-level DATASET here: a step env overrides the job env,
          # and a steps.* ref to the setup job's family step evaluates
          # EMPTY — harbor died with "Dataset  not found" (run 38126875911).
          # DATASET comes from the bench job's env block above
          # (needs.setup.outputs.dataset).
          AGENT_TIMEOUT: ${{ inputs.agent-timeout }}
          PROGRESS_EXTENSION: ${{ inputs.progress-extension }}
          # gh-1556 AC2: progress-watch is the bench default on EVERY
          # shard (#1392/#1430) — the gap-aware kill decision replaces
          # the retired byte-growth ladder that guillotined productive
          # trials (TB 2.0 Class C). FA_STALL_GAP_SEC pins the gh-1430
          # invariant (never below fa's 300s stream-idle watchdog +
          # margin — the REG in test_fa_agent_timeout.py reads the Dart
          # source and fails on drift); the abs ceiling is flat 3600s.
          # Removing these exports is the only way back to the legacy
          # ladder (its round-2 byte-for-byte REG stays green).
          # FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1 is required with the watch: without
          # it ProgressWatch degenerates to the flat base cap (the watch
          # only arms its gap-aware decision under the extension).
          FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION: '1'
          FA_STALL_GAP_SEC: '360'
          FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC: '3600'
          # shard task names: dataset dir names, no whitespace — safe to word-split.
          SHARD_TASKS: ${{ matrix.tasks }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-1503 defense-in-depth behind the setup preflight: the
          # resolved key env var must carry the selected provider's key
          # (indirect expansion — the name came from the resolve step).
          provider_key="${FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV:?resolve step did not run}"
          provider_key_value="${!provider_key}"
          [ -n "$provider_key_value" ] || { echo "::error::provider key env $provider_key is empty — the selected provider's bench secret is not set"; exit 1; }
          if [ "$ENV_TYPE" = modal ]; then
            [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_ID" ] && [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET" ] || { echo '::error::Modal secrets are not set'; exit 1; }
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded; GitHub
          # auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form too.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$provider_key_value" | base64 -w0)"
          args=()
          for t in $SHARD_TASKS; do args+=(-i "$t"); done
          # Issue #1122 knobs, same env contract as bench.yml (shared
          # bench/fa_agent_timeout.py). gh-1556 AC2: the watch knobs now
          # ride the step env block on every shard (progress-watch is the
          # bench default), so the adapter always supervises — only
          # removing those exports restores the unsupervised run. The
          # input-derived exports below still win where they are set.
          # A ceiling beyond a task's declared cap is
          # clipped by harbor's own per-task timeout (min of the two wins).
          if [ -n "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" ]; then
            case "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" in *[!0-9]*)
              echo '::error::agent-timeout must be integer seconds'; exit 1;; esac
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC="$AGENT_TIMEOUT"
          fi
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            ''|0|1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on|false|FALSE|False|no|off) ;;
            *) echo "::error::progress-extension must be boolean (true/false), got '$PROGRESS_EXTENSION'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on) export FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1;;
          esac
          # Pinned --job-name: one jobs/<name>/ dir per shard, so the summary
          # job's downloads cannot collide on harbor's timestamped default.
          # The family label keys results per dataset version (fa-4.0-*
          # matches the historical 4.0 names exactly).
          .bench-venv/bin/harbor run -d "$DATASET" -a fa_agent:FaAgent \
            -e "$ENV_TYPE" -m "$MODEL" -k "$ATTEMPTS" -n "$NCONC" \
            --job-name "fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${{ matrix.kind }}-${{ matrix.i }}" -o jobs \
            "${args[@]}"

      - name: Upload harbor job (shard ${{ matrix.i }})
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: harbor-job-shard-${{ matrix.i }}
          path: jobs/

      - name: Upload to Harbor Hub
        if: always() && env.HARBOR_API_KEY != ''
        env:
          HARBOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.HARBOR_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          shopt -s nullglob
          for job_dir in jobs/fa-${FAMILY}-*; do
            .bench-venv/bin/harbor upload "$job_dir" --public
          done

  summary:
    name: Aggregate resolution rate
    needs: [setup, bench]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Download shard results
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: harbor-job-shard-*
          merge-multiple: true
          path: jobs

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # harbor exits 0 even with unresolved trials; the verdict here covers
      # run completeness — every expected trial attempted — after the merged
      # artifact below is uploaded.
      - name: Upload merged harbor jobs
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: harbor-jobs-merged
          path: jobs/

      - name: Resolution summary & verdict
        if: always()
        env:
          EXPECTED_TASKS: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.count }}
          ATTEMPTS: ${{ inputs.attempts }}
          FAMILY: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}
          # gh-1503: pinned to the setup resolve step's outputs — the
          # free-text model input is gone; provider+model is derived
          # from the provider choice (same contract as bench.yml).
          MODEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.bench_model }}
          # gh-1503: the report names the provider+model — glm and kimi
          # runs never blend in the ledger/cost views.
          BENCH_RUN_LABEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.run_label }}
          FA_REF: ${{ github.sha }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          expected_trials=$((EXPECTED_TASKS * ATTEMPTS))
          python bench/harbor_fa/summary.py --family "$FAMILY" \
            --model "$MODEL" --fa-ref "$FA_REF" --run-url "$RUN_URL" \
            --expected-trials "$expected_trials" jobs
'

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1559
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1559
- **Title**: gh-1556 [GOAL] bench pipeline stops bleeding score: pkill self-match, progress-watch default, honest aggregate + fa deadline awareness
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1556` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 33
- **Additions**: +2383
- **Deletions**: -54
- **Created**: 2026-10-11T22:12:05Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-11T22:42:43Z

## PR Description

Closes #1556
### What changed
Bench pipeline (gh-1556): the harbor ladder kill is self-match-proof (`pkill -f '[f]a --session-root'` + a wrapped kill that can never replace the `TimeoutError` or skip the audit); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s, extension on) is the `bench-harbor.yml` default on every shard and the harbor adapter now picks the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` like the terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by `result.json` presence (errored trials get their own breakdown line, exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders table + errored breakdown + ledger row to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`. fa core: deadline awareness — `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` env, `--timer/--deadline`, and `/timer` write one session clock (`SessionDeadline`, pure Dart, injected clock); while armed every LLM request carries a per-turn `time-left:` line and one-shot `<system-notice>` steerings fire at ~50%, T-3min (wrap-up + drain background jobs), and T-30s; the TUI status line shows a countdown chip. Both bench adapters export `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) and audit the exact value. Unarmed = byte-for-byte today's behavior (REG-tested).

### Key decisions
- Deadline comes only from the adapter's own cap — with no knob there is no export (dataset caps are harbor's own; fa never invents a clock); tiny caps clamp to a 30s wrap-up window instead of landing in the past.
- The harbor deadline is stashed once at run start so the exported env value and the `fa-timeout-metadata.json` audit field are identical.
- The tb adapter rides the deadline on the launch line itself (the gh-1406 pane-env-loss lesson), not only `_env`.
- `SessionDeadline` reuses the existing `SessionVarsExecutionEnv` seam (live per exec) rather than adding a second env provider.
- AC9 (no full 2.1 dispatch before a green smoke) is a process gate, not code — documented in `docs/bench.md`.

### How to verify
```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench   # 356 ok
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa        # 77 ok
dart analyze                                           # 0 errors/warnings
dart test test/session_deadline_test.dart test/agent/session_deadline_loop_test.dart \
  test/cli/agent_cli_timer_test.dart                   # 32/32
```
Full `dart test` note: the monolithic run passed 7448 tests but the runner's Dart VM aborted twice with a native `malloc_consolidate` crash under sustained load; all 22 recorded failures are ambient-env leaks (`FA_LOG_FILE`/`FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` exported by the dev-runner harness) or load flakes — every failing file re-runs green individually with a sanitized env (incl. `origin/main` failing the boot-perf test identically here).

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  ENV[FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS host env] --> SD[SessionDeadline — one clock]
  FLAG[fa --timer/--deadline] --> SD
  SLASH[TUI /timer] --> SD
  SD --> CTX[per-turn time-left: request line]
  SD --> NOTICE[one-shot system notices 50% / T-3min / T-30s]
  SD --> CHIP[TUI countdown chip — pure projection]
  SD --> BASH[bash env via SessionVarsExecutionEnv — live per exec]
  CAP[adapter effective kill cap] --> DEADLINE[FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS = cap − 120s]
  DEADLINE --> ENV
```
</details>

```dart
void _validateDeadlineFlags() {

    );
  }
  _validateDeadlineFlag(timer, '--timer');
  _validateDeadlineFlag(deadline, '--deadline');
}
```

and replace the three statements in `finish()` with a single `_validateDeadlineFlags();` call — restoring CC to 12.

# gh-1556: [GOAL] bench pipeline stops bleeding score: pkill self-match, progress-watch default, honest aggregate + fa deadline awareness

## Description

## One-line

The TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding run (59/79 = 74.7%) proved the measurement pipeline bleeds score and trust on three independent defects — a self-matching `pkill` that misclassifies kills as agent crashes (a SOLVED task scored 0), the retired #1392 legacy timeout ladder still running because the workflow never enables progress-watch, an aggregate that reddens on legitimate dataset-cap timeouts with no visible summary — and that fa itself is blind to wall-clock budgets, dying at caps mid-work instead of landing partial results.

## Measured evidence — TB 2.0, run 38150649548 (fa@d6fb13e2e)

Full-log RCA of all 10 errored trials (`harbor-jobs-merged` artifact):

**Class A — pkill self-match bug (3 trials, all at the 1440s hard-ceiling):**
`winning-avg-corewars`, `path-tracing`, `extract-moves-from-video`.
`exception.txt`: `NonZeroAgentExitCodeError: Command failed (exit 143): pkill -f 'fa --session-root' || true`. The `exec_as_root` wrapper's own cmdline contains the pattern → `pkill -f` SIGTERMs its own shell → exit 143 propagates out of the ladder kill block in `bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py::_run_with_deadline`, skipping the audit write AND the `TimeoutError` raise → harbor records an agent crash. **Direct score loss: `extract-moves-from-video` had reward 1.0 but was excluded as errored** (74.7% → 76.0% on this alone).

**Class B — dataset-declared per-task caps (5-6 trials, harbor-native `_run_agent_phase wait_for`, round 15/20/25 min, no audit file):**
`caffe-cifar-10` (20:00.00), `qemu-alpine-ssh` (15:00.00), `write-compressor` (15:00.00), `make-doom-for-mips` (15:00.00), `cobol-modernization` (15:00.00), likely `make-mips-interpreter` (25:00.00). Harbor enforces the task's own cap — NOT our ladder. These caps are part of the leaderboard measurement; we do NOT override them (comparability).

**Class C — our legacy ladder hard-ceiling (1 confirmed):**
`protein-assembly` (25:00), audit: `outcome: hard-ceiling, ceiling_multiplier 4.0, ceiling_sec 1440`. The bench ran the round-2 `ProgressLadder` because progress-watch (#1392/#1430: stall-gap + abs ceiling 3600s) only activates when `FA_STALL_GAP_SEC`/`FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC` are set — and `bench-harbor.yml` never sets them. The ×4 ceiling is the exact mechanism #1392 retired as "the killer".

**Aggregate redness:** `summary.py` exits 1 when attempted < expected (89); errored trials count as unattempted → legit timeouts redden the job. By design as a lost-shard guard, but misfires on the errored class.

**Summary visibility:** TB1's workflow surfaced the resolution summary in the job output; bench-harbor's aggregate only uploads artifacts — reading the result requires downloading 34 MB.

**fa-side gap behind Class B:** agents died at caps while productively working — fa has no deadline signal, so it cannot shift into wrap-up (land partial results, run checks, exit 0). This is the temporal sibling of the FinalizeGate (gh-1412): finalize-gate checks answer completeness; deadline awareness checks session completeness against a clock.

## Acceptance criteria

**Bench harness (bench/harbor_fa, workflow):**
1. **pkill self-match eliminated** (`fa_agent.py`): bracket-trick (`[f]a --session-root`) or equivalent + the best-effort kill wrapped so its failure can never replace the ladder's `TimeoutError`; REG test: self-matching wrapper still classifies as timeout and still writes the audit record.
2. **Progress-watch is the bench default**: `bench-harbor.yml` sets the knobs for every shard (stall-gap per the gh-1430 invariant — never below fa's 300s stream-idle watchdog + margin; abs ceiling 3600s). Legacy ladder reachable only by explicit knob removal (round-2 byte-for-byte REG stays green).
3. **Aggregate completeness by presence**: a trial with a readable `result.json` counts as attempted regardless of exception class; errored trials report as their own breakdown line; exit 1 ONLY on genuinely lost trials (no result.json) — the lost-shard guard keeps its teeth.
4. **Summary surfaced**: aggregate writes the resolution table + errored breakdown + ledger row to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity) in addition to artifacts.

**fa core (deadline awareness):**
5. **Deadline signal — three entry points, one clock**:
   - hosts inject `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (env, resolved live per turn via the session-correlation seam);
   - CLI flag `fa --timer 25m` / `--deadline <duration|epoch>` (headless AND interactive — the flag just sets the same env for the session);
   - TUI slash-command `/timer 25m` (set/adjust/clear mid-session) with a countdown chip in the status area while armed.
   Absent/cleared = today's behavior byte-for-byte (REG: prompt, records, events unchanged).
6. **Budget surfacing + wrap-up steering**: every LLM request context carries the remaining budget as a small per-turn line (e.g. `time-left: 5min`, refreshed per turn — the context builder already injects live session facts); one-shot system notices at the configured crossings ride the existing system-notice machinery — default ladder: ~50% ("half the budget gone"), **T-3min mandatory steer: "stop exploring, finalize outputs, drain/kill background jobs, run your checks"** (long-running operations must be given their chance to land — shell-job drain, file flushes), T-30s "write final answer NOW"; headless `fa -p` finishes the wrap-up turn and exits 0 instead of dying mid-tool-call.
7. **Bench wiring**: both bench adapters (`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py`, `bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py`) export the deadline from the effective cap minus a small safety margin.

**Cross-cutting:**
8. Dataset-declared task caps, scoring semantics, and the harbor contract unchanged; TDD; >90% coverage on new code; existing `test_fa_agent_timeout.py` / `test_bench_harbor_workflow.py` REGs green; docs (bench + env reference) + CHANGELOG.
9. **Gate for the TB 2.1 run**: no full 2.1 dispatch until this lands and a smoke dispatch (`family=2.0, tasks=<smoke task>`) shows a green aggregate with a rendered step summary.

## Threats / design notes

- **Comparability**: deadline awareness is agent capability, not cap evasion — the cap is unchanged; harbor still enforces. Leaderboard agents with native budget handling benefit equivalently.
- **Never lie about the clock**: the deadline comes only from host env; fa never invents or extends it; missing/invalid = feature off.
- **Not a procrastination loop**: notices fire once per crossing; the model may ignore them; the guillotine stays the host's.
- **One clock, three setters**: env, `--timer/--deadline`, and `/timer` write the same single session value; later setters override earlier ones; the TUI chip is a pure projection (no second timer source).
- **T-3min is the load-bearing crossing**: it exists so long operations (compiles, uploads, background shell jobs) are drained deliberately rather than SIGKILLed mid-write — the wrap-up steer must name the drain explicitly.
- Pure-Dart core: env read behind existing env seams; no `dart:io` in `lib/`.

## Non-goals

- Raising/overriding dataset task caps (breaks leaderboard comparability).
- Scoring changes (resolved = every verifier reward 1.0 stays).
- Per-task adaptive caps learned from history (separate discussion).

## Test plan

- UT: pkill non-self-match + kill-path classification; completeness counting with synthetic errored/lost trials; workflow knob wiring (`test_bench_harbor_workflow.py`); deadline resolution from all three entry points (env/flag/slash) with override order; per-turn `time-left` prompt line; crossing notices (incl. the T-3min drain steer) with fake clock + scripted loop; TUI countdown chip render; headless clean-exit.
- REG: gh-1430 watchdog-gap invariant; legacy ladder byte-for-byte without knobs; deadline-unset byte-for-byte.
- IT: smoke dispatch post-merge — aggregate green, step summary rendered, audit present, deadline env visible in `fa-timeout-metadata.json`.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

          # shard (#1392/#1430) — the gap-aware kill decision replaces
          # the retired byte-growth ladder that guillotined productive
          # trials (TB 2.0 Class C). FA_STALL_GAP_SEC pins the gh-1430

          # source and fails on drift); the abs ceiling is flat 3600s.
          # Removing these exports is the only way back to the legacy
          # ladder (its round-2 byte-for-byte REG stays green).
          # FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1 is required with the watch: without
          # it ProgressWatch degenerates to the flat base cap (the watch
          # only arms its gap-aware decision under the extension).
          FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION: '1'
          FA_STALL_GAP_SEC: '360'
          FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC: '3600'
          # shard task names: dataset dir names, no whitespace — safe to word-split.
          SHARD_TASKS: ${{ matrix.tasks }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-1503 defense-in-depth behind the setup preflight: the
          # resolved key env var must carry the selected provider's key

          provider_key="${FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV:?resolve step did not run}"
          provider_key_value="${!provider_key}"
          [ -n "$provider_key_value" ] || { echo "::error::provider key env $provider_key is empty — the selected provider's bench secret is not set"; exit 1; }
          if [ "$ENV_TYPE" = modal ]; then
            [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_ID" ] && [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET" ] || { echo '::error::Modal secrets are not set'; exit 1; }

name: Bench Harbor

# Runs the fa coding agent against the Terminal-Bench dataset family on
# the Harbor framework: 2.0 / 2.1 / 3.0 / 4.0 from ONE dispatch surface
# (issue #1124; the 4.0 path is issue #147). The `dataset` input takes a
# family label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or a full Harbor dataset id — resolved
# and validated by bench/harbor_fa/families.py (unknown or version-less
# specs fail fast; never a silent fallback). The default dispatch is the
# 2.1 family (issue #1316: the bench migrates to Terminal-Bench 2.x /
# Harbor — supersedes #1124 AC4's 4.0 default; 4.0/3.0/2.0 stay one input
# away). CPU shards run the default Harbor `docker` sandbox on
# ubuntu-latest (GH runners ship docker — no Modal/cloud dependency for
# the default dispatch, #1316); GPU tasks always route to a modal shard
# and cpu-runner/cpu-env keep the self-hosted + modal dispatch reachable.
# Results upload
# to Harbor Hub — the current leaderboard source (tbench.ai; 4.0 is the
# leaderboard dataset). The legacy terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 path lives
# in bench.yml.
#
# Same bundle/env contract as the legacy bench: `dart build cli` Linux
# bundle + an env-provider-preconfig, secrets env-only and never echoed
# (keys pass base64-encoded into the task container; CI masks both raw
# and base64 forms).
#
# gh-1503: the provider is no longer a z.ai hardcode — the dispatch
# picks zai glm-5.3-flash (default, byte-identical to the pre-gh-1503
# wiring), kimi-for-coding k3-256k (FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY), or `custom`
# (provider-config JSON validated in the resolve step; key only from
# FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY). The setup job's resolve step is a byte-consistent
# copy of bench.yml's gh-1471 step — keep both in sync (cross-reference
# comment in both files). With the z.ai budget at zero, the kimi path is
# what keeps this workflow dispatchable.
#
# Smoke first: dispatch with tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1 (smoke task
# per family in docs/bench.md). Full (tasks-less) runs of the
# intermediate families (2.0/2.1/3.0) additionally require
# confirm-full-run: true — a full family sweep is hours of GPU + LLM
# spend. Full 4.0 dispatches keep their historical no-confirmation
# behaviour (issue #1124 AC4).
#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY       — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
#   FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY      — kimi coding key for k3-256k (shared with bench.yml;
#                            never the review factory's KIMI_REVIEW_KEY)
#   FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY    — key for provider=custom, injected as FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
#   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET  — Modal token for the GPU shard (verified live)
#   HARBOR_API_KEY         — Harbor Hub upload key; upload step skips (with a
#                            warning) when absent, run artifacts keep results.

run-name: fa bench-harbor · ${{ inputs.provider }} · ${{ inputs.tasks }}

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset (empty = full dataset; use the family smoke task first — docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1503, same contract as bench.yml gh-1471: default = pre-gh-1503 behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret; custom needs FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY + provider-config)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
          - 'custom'
      provider-config:
        description: 'gh-1503 (bench.yml gh-1471 D1/AC 2a): ONLY when provider=custom — the provider config JSON {"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}. The API key NEVER rides this input (run metadata is visible) — it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Terminal-Bench family: label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or full Harbor id (see bench/harbor_fa/families.py); default 2.1 (issue #1316)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest'
      confirm-full-run:
        description: 'Required true for full (tasks-less) runs of 2.0/2.1/3.0 — smoke first (docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false

def _resolve_run_block() -> str:
    """Extracts the `run: |` block of the provider resolve step.

    Same text-slicing contract as bench/terminal_bench/test_bench_workflow.py
    (_resolve_run_block): the block is identified by its body (the
    provider_config printf), so unrelated `run:` blocks never match. The
    block is env-driven (inputs/secrets arrive via the step env), so no
    GitHub expression may appear inside.
    """
    lines = _HARBOR_YML.read_text().splitlines()
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if line.strip() != "run: |":
            continue
        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
        body = []
        for candidate in lines[i + 1 :]:
            if candidate.strip() and (len(candidate) - len(candidate.lstrip())) <= indent:
                break
            body.append(candidate)
        while body and not body[-1].strip():
            body.pop()
        block = "\n".join(body)
        if "provider_config=$(printf" in block:
            break
    else:
        raise AssertionError("provider resolve step's run: | block not found in bench-harbor.yml")
    leftover = re.findall(r"\$\{\{[^}]*\}\}", block)
    assert not leftover, f"unmapped GitHub expression(s) in resolve block: {leftover}"
    return block


def _bench_yml_resolve_block() -> str:

def _input_default(workflow_text: str, name: str):
    """Reads `default:` from one workflow_dispatch input block (stdlib)."""
    m = re.search(
        rf"^      {re.escape(name)}:\n((?:        .*\n)+)", workflow_text, re.M
    )
    if not m:
        return None
    d = re.search(r"^\s+default: (.+)$", m.group(1), re.M)
    if not d:
        return None
    return d.group(1).strip().strip("'")


def _workflow_input(workflow_text: str, name: str):
    value = _input_default(workflow_text, name)
    if value is None:
        raise AssertionError(f"input `{name}` has no default in the workflow")
    return value

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1559
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1559
- **Title**: gh-1556 [GOAL] bench pipeline stops bleeding score: pkill self-match, progress-watch default, honest aggregate + fa deadline awareness
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1556` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 33
- **Additions**: +2383
- **Deletions**: -54
- **Created**: 2026-10-11T22:12:05Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-11T22:42:43Z

## PR Description

Closes #1556
### What changed
Bench pipeline (gh-1556): the harbor ladder kill is self-match-proof (`pkill -f '[f]a --session-root'` + a wrapped kill that can never replace the `TimeoutError` or skip the audit); progress-watch (stall-gap 360s per the gh-1430 watchdog invariant, flat abs ceiling 3600s, extension on) is the `bench-harbor.yml` default on every shard and the harbor adapter now picks the gap-aware `ProgressWatch` like the terminal-bench adapter; the aggregate counts completeness by `result.json` presence (errored trials get their own breakdown line, exit 1 only on genuinely lost trials) and renders table + errored breakdown + ledger row to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`. fa core: deadline awareness — `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` env, `--timer/--deadline`, and `/timer` write one session clock (`SessionDeadline`, pure Dart, injected clock); while armed every LLM request carries a per-turn `time-left:` line and one-shot `<system-notice>` steerings fire at ~50%, T-3min (wrap-up + drain background jobs), and T-30s; the TUI status line shows a countdown chip. Both bench adapters export `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (effective cap − 120s wrap-up margin) and audit the exact value. Unarmed = byte-for-byte today's behavior (REG-tested).

### Key decisions
- Deadline comes only from the adapter's own cap — with no knob there is no export (dataset caps are harbor's own; fa never invents a clock); tiny caps clamp to a 30s wrap-up window instead of landing in the past.
- The harbor deadline is stashed once at run start so the exported env value and the `fa-timeout-metadata.json` audit field are identical.
- The tb adapter rides the deadline on the launch line itself (the gh-1406 pane-env-loss lesson), not only `_env`.
- `SessionDeadline` reuses the existing `SessionVarsExecutionEnv` seam (live per exec) rather than adding a second env provider.
- AC9 (no full 2.1 dispatch before a green smoke) is a process gate, not code — documented in `docs/bench.md`.

### How to verify
```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench   # 356 ok
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa        # 77 ok
dart analyze                                           # 0 errors/warnings
dart test test/session_deadline_test.dart test/agent/session_deadline_loop_test.dart \
  test/cli/agent_cli_timer_test.dart                   # 32/32
```
Full `dart test` note: the monolithic run passed 7448 tests but the runner's Dart VM aborted twice with a native `malloc_consolidate` crash under sustained load; all 22 recorded failures are ambient-env leaks (`FA_LOG_FILE`/`FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` exported by the dev-runner harness) or load flakes — every failing file re-runs green individually with a sanitized env (incl. `origin/main` failing the boot-perf test identically here).

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  ENV[FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS host env] --> SD[SessionDeadline — one clock]
  FLAG[fa --timer/--deadline] --> SD
  SLASH[TUI /timer] --> SD
  SD --> CTX[per-turn time-left: request line]
  SD --> NOTICE[one-shot system notices 50% / T-3min / T-30s]
  SD --> CHIP[TUI countdown chip — pure projection]
  SD --> BASH[bash env via SessionVarsExecutionEnv — live per exec]
  CAP[adapter effective kill cap] --> DEADLINE[FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS = cap − 120s]
  DEADLINE --> ENV
```
</details>

# gh-1556: [GOAL] bench pipeline stops bleeding score: pkill self-match, progress-watch default, honest aggregate + fa deadline awareness

## Description

## One-line

The TB 2.0 × kimi-for-coding run (59/79 = 74.7%) proved the measurement pipeline bleeds score and trust on three independent defects — a self-matching `pkill` that misclassifies kills as agent crashes (a SOLVED task scored 0), the retired #1392 legacy timeout ladder still running because the workflow never enables progress-watch, an aggregate that reddens on legitimate dataset-cap timeouts with no visible summary — and that fa itself is blind to wall-clock budgets, dying at caps mid-work instead of landing partial results.

## Measured evidence — TB 2.0, run 38150649548 (fa@d6fb13e2e)

Full-log RCA of all 10 errored trials (`harbor-jobs-merged` artifact):

**Class A — pkill self-match bug (3 trials, all at the 1440s hard-ceiling):**
`winning-avg-corewars`, `path-tracing`, `extract-moves-from-video`.
`exception.txt`: `NonZeroAgentExitCodeError: Command failed (exit 143): pkill -f 'fa --session-root' || true`. The `exec_as_root` wrapper's own cmdline contains the pattern → `pkill -f` SIGTERMs its own shell → exit 143 propagates out of the ladder kill block in `bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py::_run_with_deadline`, skipping the audit write AND the `TimeoutError` raise → harbor records an agent crash. **Direct score loss: `extract-moves-from-video` had reward 1.0 but was excluded as errored** (74.7% → 76.0% on this alone).

**Class B — dataset-declared per-task caps (5-6 trials, harbor-native `_run_agent_phase wait_for`, round 15/20/25 min, no audit file):**
`caffe-cifar-10` (20:00.00), `qemu-alpine-ssh` (15:00.00), `write-compressor` (15:00.00), `make-doom-for-mips` (15:00.00), `cobol-modernization` (15:00.00), likely `make-mips-interpreter` (25:00.00). Harbor enforces the task's own cap — NOT our ladder. These caps are part of the leaderboard measurement; we do NOT override them (comparability).

**Class C — our legacy ladder hard-ceiling (1 confirmed):**
`protein-assembly` (25:00), audit: `outcome: hard-ceiling, ceiling_multiplier 4.0, ceiling_sec 1440`. The bench ran the round-2 `ProgressLadder` because progress-watch (#1392/#1430: stall-gap + abs ceiling 3600s) only activates when `FA_STALL_GAP_SEC`/`FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC` are set — and `bench-harbor.yml` never sets them. The ×4 ceiling is the exact mechanism #1392 retired as "the killer".

**Aggregate redness:** `summary.py` exits 1 when attempted < expected (89); errored trials count as unattempted → legit timeouts redden the job. By design as a lost-shard guard, but misfires on the errored class.

**Summary visibility:** TB1's workflow surfaced the resolution summary in the job output; bench-harbor's aggregate only uploads artifacts — reading the result requires downloading 34 MB.

**fa-side gap behind Class B:** agents died at caps while productively working — fa has no deadline signal, so it cannot shift into wrap-up (land partial results, run checks, exit 0). This is the temporal sibling of the FinalizeGate (gh-1412): finalize-gate checks answer completeness; deadline awareness checks session completeness against a clock.

## Acceptance criteria

**Bench harness (bench/harbor_fa, workflow):**
1. **pkill self-match eliminated** (`fa_agent.py`): bracket-trick (`[f]a --session-root`) or equivalent + the best-effort kill wrapped so its failure can never replace the ladder's `TimeoutError`; REG test: self-matching wrapper still classifies as timeout and still writes the audit record.
2. **Progress-watch is the bench default**: `bench-harbor.yml` sets the knobs for every shard (stall-gap per the gh-1430 invariant — never below fa's 300s stream-idle watchdog + margin; abs ceiling 3600s). Legacy ladder reachable only by explicit knob removal (round-2 byte-for-byte REG stays green).
3. **Aggregate completeness by presence**: a trial with a readable `result.json` counts as attempted regardless of exception class; errored trials report as their own breakdown line; exit 1 ONLY on genuinely lost trials (no result.json) — the lost-shard guard keeps its teeth.
4. **Summary surfaced**: aggregate writes the resolution table + errored breakdown + ledger row to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (TB1 parity) in addition to artifacts.

**fa core (deadline awareness):**
5. **Deadline signal — three entry points, one clock**:
   - hosts inject `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (env, resolved live per turn via the session-correlation seam);
   - CLI flag `fa --timer 25m` / `--deadline <duration|epoch>` (headless AND interactive — the flag just sets the same env for the session);
   - TUI slash-command `/timer 25m` (set/adjust/clear mid-session) with a countdown chip in the status area while armed.
   Absent/cleared = today's behavior byte-for-byte (REG: prompt, records, events unchanged).
6. **Budget surfacing + wrap-up steering**: every LLM request context carries the remaining budget as a small per-turn line (e.g. `time-left: 5min`, refreshed per turn — the context builder already injects live session facts); one-shot system notices at the configured crossings ride the existing system-notice machinery — default ladder: ~50% ("half the budget gone"), **T-3min mandatory steer: "stop exploring, finalize outputs, drain/kill background jobs, run your checks"** (long-running operations must be given their chance to land — shell-job drain, file flushes), T-30s "write final answer NOW"; headless `fa -p` finishes the wrap-up turn and exits 0 instead of dying mid-tool-call.
7. **Bench wiring**: both bench adapters (`bench/harbor_fa/fa_agent.py`, `bench/terminal_bench/fa_agent.py`) export the deadline from the effective cap minus a small safety margin.

**Cross-cutting:**
8. Dataset-declared task caps, scoring semantics, and the harbor contract unchanged; TDD; >90% coverage on new code; existing `test_fa_agent_timeout.py` / `test_bench_harbor_workflow.py` REGs green; docs (bench + env reference) + CHANGELOG.
9. **Gate for the TB 2.1 run**: no full 2.1 dispatch until this lands and a smoke dispatch (`family=2.0, tasks=<smoke task>`) shows a green aggregate with a rendered step summary.

## Threats / design notes

- **Comparability**: deadline awareness is agent capability, not cap evasion — the cap is unchanged; harbor still enforces. Leaderboard agents with native budget handling benefit equivalently.
- **Never lie about the clock**: the deadline comes only from host env; fa never invents or extends it; missing/invalid = feature off.
- **Not a procrastination loop**: notices fire once per crossing; the model may ignore them; the guillotine stays the host's.
- **One clock, three setters**: env, `--timer/--deadline`, and `/timer` write the same single session value; later setters override earlier ones; the TUI chip is a pure projection (no second timer source).
- **T-3min is the load-bearing crossing**: it exists so long operations (compiles, uploads, background shell jobs) are drained deliberately rather than SIGKILLed mid-write — the wrap-up steer must name the drain explicitly.
- Pure-Dart core: env read behind existing env seams; no `dart:io` in `lib/`.

## Non-goals

- Raising/overriding dataset task caps (breaks leaderboard comparability).
- Scoring changes (resolved = every verifier reward 1.0 stays).
- Per-task adaptive caps learned from history (separate discussion).

## Test plan

- UT: pkill non-self-match + kill-path classification; completeness counting with synthetic errored/lost trials; workflow knob wiring (`test_bench_harbor_workflow.py`); deadline resolution from all three entry points (env/flag/slash) with override order; per-turn `time-left` prompt line; crossing notices (incl. the T-3min drain steer) with fake clock + scripted loop; TUI countdown chip render; headless clean-exit.
- REG: gh-1430 watchdog-gap invariant; legacy ladder byte-for-byte without knobs; deadline-unset byte-for-byte.
- IT: smoke dispatch post-merge — aggregate green, step summary rendered, audit present, deadline env visible in `fa-timeout-metadata.json`.

## Machine jobs
- [x] ▶ dev (fa-story-dev) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/381709…

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…
